name: Finn Jones
headline: Associate Software Engineer at Lendi Group
positioning: A software engineer who speaks finance.
subheadline: Building modern web and software products — currently reading Computer Science & Commerce (Finance) at UNSW.
about: I'm an engineer with a dual degree in Computer Science and Commerce (Finance) from UNSW. I pair technical depth with a working understanding of markets and money — which is how I ended up building software in the mortgage and lending space at Lendi Group.

My path runs from IT support managing thousands of devices, through freelance development for small businesses, to enterprise software engineering. That range means I'm comfortable from low-level infrastructure up to the polished edge users actually touch.

highlights: Building and maintaining software products across the mortgage and lending space
Shipping with modern web technologies inside agile, cross-functional teams
Managed 2,000+ devices with JAMF — performance, security, and minimal downtime
Automated device management, cutting manual work and lifting team efficiency
Resolved support tickets fast, keeping staff and students productive
Strong stakeholder management across students, teachers, and parents
Custom web design, client training, and project delivery for small businesses

projects.title: AGLC4 Citation Tool
projects.summary: A formatter that rewrites legal citations in Word essays to the AGLC4 standard.
projects.problem: The Australian Guide to Legal Citation runs to hundreds of rules, and law students hand-format every footnote by eye — slow, inconsistent, and easy to get wrong the night before a deadline.
projects.approach: A Python tool that parses citations inside a Word document, matches them against AGLC4 rules, and rewrites them in place — preserving the document structure while fixing punctuation, ordering, and style.
projects.outcome: Turns an hour of manual citation cleanup into a single pass, so the work goes into the argument instead of the footnotes.

projects.title: LiftLink
projects.summary: A web app that automatically merges duplicate Strava activities.
projects.problem: Athletes who record the same session on more than one device end up with duplicate activities cluttering their Strava feed, throwing off totals and stats.
projects.approach: Connect once with Strava via OAuth, detect overlapping activities by time and distance, and merge the duplicates — no manual deleting, no spreadsheet.
projects.outcome: A clean, accurate activity history maintained automatically after a single connection.

projects.title: Votencrypt
projects.summary: A blockchain voting platform built on DAML smart contracts.
projects.problem: Digital voting has to prove two things at once that usually fight each other: every vote is counted exactly once, and no one can see how an individual voted.
projects.approach: A voting platform modelled as DAML smart contracts, so the rules of an election — eligibility, one vote per voter, tallying — are enforced by the ledger itself rather than by a trusted server.
projects.outcome: A working, verifiable voting system and my Year 12 Software Development major work, published at votencrypt.com.

projects.title: AchieveIt Bookings
projects.summary: An online booking system for a private tutoring company.
projects.problem: A tutoring business was coordinating sessions over back-and-forth messages, with no single place for clients to see availability and book.
projects.approach: A self-serve booking flow where clients pick a slot and confirm online, giving the business a clear schedule and fewer scheduling conflicts.
projects.outcome: Live booking for AchieveIt's clients, cutting the admin overhead of arranging each session by hand.

projects.title: Trading Game
projects.summary: A stock-trading simulator driven by live market data.
projects.problem: Learning how markets behave is expensive and slow if the only way to practise is with real money.
projects.approach: A Python game that pulls live prices through the Yahoo Finance API and runs a paper-trading loop — buy, sell, and track a simulated portfolio against real market movements.
projects.outcome: A safe sandbox for building market intuition, and the project where my CS and finance interests first met in code.

projects.title: Trigger Outlaws
projects.summary: A tile-based, top-down RPG built with pygame.
projects.problem: A team project to design and ship a complete game loop — movement, combat, levels, and win state — within a course deadline.
projects.approach: Built a top-down, tile-based RPG in pygame with a small team, dividing systems across movement, encounters, and level design.
projects.outcome: A finished, playable game and a lesson in shipping real software collaboratively under version control.
